reason: All 28 oxlint-only reports are CommonJS bindings named like builtins (escape, Symbol, Promise, a few inside nested functions) that oxlint's builtinGlobals check treats as global redeclarations, while ESLint checks only the global scope; all 19 ESLint-only reports come from /* global X */ comments redeclaring builtins, which oxlint does not read.
evidence: ESLint doc: 'check for redeclaration of built-in globals in global scope ... [with] sourceType commonjs ... declaring a variable named after a builtin global is not a redeclaration'. oxc #18253 (open, 'Handling CommonJS ... clashes with globals can't happen'), PR #27029 (open, 'The builtin/global-name check runs for every symbol, including symbols in nested scopes'); /* global */ gap: #12648 (open), #18308 ('Oxlint doesn't support /* global */ comments'). Repro: function f(){ let escape = false } -> oxlint reports, ESLint not.

reason: 33 of the 36 ESLint-only reports are .replace(REGEX_CONST, ...) where unicorn resolves a constant /…/g variable statically (it has done so since at least v63) and oxlint checks only inline regex literals and new RegExp(...), a gap known to the porters (unicorn's test is commented out) but with no tracker issue; the rest is LAG: split().join() (unicorn v65 #3048), the RegExp-escape exemption (v68 #3367) and non-static new RegExp(x, 'g') (unicorn >=v74), which give the 6 oxlint-only reports.
evidence: Repro: const RE = /a/g; s.replace(RE, 'b') -> ESLint reports, oxlint not. oxlint_v1.88.0 prefer_string_replace_all.rs keeps unicorn's case commented out: // r#"const pattern = new RegExp("foo", "g"); foo.replace(pattern, bar)"#. LAG part: s.replace(/[|\\{}()[\]^$+*?.]/g, '\\$&') -> oxlint only (unicorn v68 skips RegExp-escape calls).

reason: oxlint compares each declarator with the one just before it, while ESLint compares with the last declarator that was in order, so ESLint reports every declarator below the running maximum and oxlint only adjacent inversions (both flag the same declarations).
evidence: Repro: var c, a, b; -> ESLint reports a and b (2), oxlint reports only a (1). ESLint sort-vars.js reduce() keeps memo on a report; oxlint sort_vars.rs always sets previous = Some(current). No tracker hit for sort-vars.

reason: All 40 reports are in qs test files that turn the rule off with /* eslint no-sparse-arrays: 0 */; ESLint (inline config on in our setup) obeys it, oxlint does not read rule-configuration comments.
evidence: oxlint docs, Inline ignore comments: 'Comments must start with one of the keywords below' (oxlint-disable/-enable/-disable-line/-disable-next-line and the eslint-* forms) and 'Rule options cannot be changed inline'; oxc #12648 (open) lists /* eslint no-alert: "off" */ style comments as unsupported. Repro: ESLint with the comment 0 reports, oxlint 1.

reason: oxlint implements unicorn <=v63 (lone throw in a block, in either branch); unicorn v77 also reports brace-less if (...) throw new Error() and ignores else branches (most ESLint-only reports), and v66 skips typeof x === 'undefined' checks (oxlint-only); secondary BUG: oxlint has no ParenthesizedExpression case, so if (!(x instanceof Y)) { throw new Error() } is missed (ajv, esbuild).
evidence: unicorn commit fc14587d (2026-09-30, in v77.0.0) 'Report a brace-less if body and ignore the else branch'; v66.0.0 #3067 'Don't flag typeof x === undefined existence checks'. Repro: if (!(v instanceof Uint8Array)) { throw new Error('bad') } -> ESLint reports, oxlint not (is_type_checking_expr in prefer_type_error.rs has no ParenthesizedExpression arm).

reason: 23 of 26 are the 'fallback expressions' reports (e.g. this.x = y || '') added in unicorn v77 (#3780) and v78 (#3837, on by default); the 3 'reassignment' cases are a secondary deviation: oxlint gives up when a call-free statement such as a = a || 1, this.x = y or x ??= {} comes first, while unicorn only gives up after a preceding call.
evidence: unicorn 78 prefer-default-parameters.js defaultOptions [{checkFallbackExpressions: true}]; release notes v77 #3780, v78 #3837. Repro: function f(a, b) { a = a || 1; b = b || 2; return [a, b] } -> ESLint reports b, oxlint nothing (is_side_effect_free_statement rejects LogicalExpression and member targets; unicorn hasSideEffects checks calls only, same in v60).

reason: oxlint's boolean-context check has no LogicalExpression case, so a .match()/.exec() that is an operand of && or || in a condition is never reported (all 22 ESLint-only, yargs-parser, brace-expansion, glob); the 4 oxlint-only are LAG: unicorn v66 type inference skips .match(knownString) such as m.match(dir + '/').
evidence: Repro: if (a && s.match(/x/)) {} and if (s.match(/x/) || a) {} -> ESLint reports both, oxlint none; prefer_regexp_test.rs matches only For/Conditional/Boolean()/While/DoWhile/If/Unary parents, unicorn's isBooleanNode accepts logical operands (unicorn v60 utils/boolean.js). No oxc tracker hit.

reason: 13 of the 15 ESLint-only reports have a receiver that is itself a member expression (this.nodes.every(fn), node.elements.forEach(this.visit, this)), which oxlint deliberately skips, and ajv's types.every(...) hits oxlint's 'types' ignore that unicorn applies only to .map; secondary: oxlint reports call-expression callbacks such as arr.forEach(make(x)) (5 oxlint-only), which unicorn has always ignored.
evidence: no_array_callback_reference.rs: '// Skip if object is a member expression (e.g., types.map, oidc.Client.find) // These are likely not array methods but methods on namespaces/classes'. unicorn (v60 to v78): '// Ignore all CallExpressions include function.bind()'. Repro: ['a'].forEach(clearItem(c)) -> oxlint only; this.nodes.every(cond) -> ESLint only.

reason: unicorn v65 also checks directory names, and all 21 reports are resolve test fixtures under snake_case directories (module_dir, node_path, browser_field); oxlint checks only the file name.
evidence: unicorn v65.0.0 release note 'filename-case: Check directories too (#3038)'. Repro: snake_dir/index.js -> ESLint 'Directory name snake_dir is not in kebab case', oxlint silent.

reason: The 12 ESLint-only reports are //oxlint-disable-next-line and // prettier-ignore comments, which oxlint skips on purpose and ESLint's default ignore pattern does not; the one oxlint-only report is /*jslint ...*/, which ESLint's default pattern skips (jslint\s+) but oxlint's directive list omits (secondary BUG).
evidence: oxc #16989 'ignore oxlint directive comments in capitalized-comments' and #19008 'ignore prettier and oxfmt directives'; ESLint COMMENTS_IGNORE_PATTERN /^\s*(?:eslint|jshint\s+|jslint\s+|istanbul\s+|globals?\s+|exported\s+|jscs)/. Repro: /*jslint node:true*/ -> oxlint reports, ESLint not.

reason: oxlint skips every + expression that has any + ancestor, even across a conditional, call or function body, whereas ESLint merges only directly chained concatenations, so nested concatenations such as a + (b ? '|' + c : '') are never reported by oxlint.
evidence: Repro: return a + (b ? "|" + c : "") and x + [1].map(function (y) { return "v" + y; }).length -> ESLint 1 report each, oxlint 0. prefer_template.rs: not_outermost = ancestor_kinds(...).any(BinaryExpression with +). No oxc tracker hit.

reason: oxlint treats a class field initializer as code that runs once, so it flags id = ++ID on a module counter (2 oxlint-only, minimatch), and it misses dead stores that ESLint finds (a chained o.p = x = f(x), the last offset++ inside one expression, an initializer overwritten in a short-circuit loop condition).
evidence: Repro: let ID = 0; class A { id = ++ID; } -> oxlint 'This assigned value is not used', ESLint nothing (function tick(){ n++ } is not flagged by either); function f(path, o) { o.path = path = path.replace(/x/, ''); return o } -> ESLint reports path, oxlint not. No open oxc issue on these shapes.

reason: All 10 ESLint-only reports are the new 'Combine this initialization with the preceding declaration' check (let x; x = value;) added in unicorn v78.
evidence: unicorn v78.0.0 release note 'no-immediate-mutation: Combine a declaration with an assignment that follows it immediately (#3851)'; the message is absent from the v77.0.0 rule source.

reason: unicorn v68 added the Error subclasses (TypeError, RangeError, ...) to the builtins that need new; oxlint's list still has only Error, so throw TypeError('...') (json5, uuid) is ESLint-only.
evidence: unicorn v68.0.0 'new-for-builtins: Cover more builtins (#3361)': enforceNew gains ...builtinErrors (v67 list has only 'Error'); oxlint new_for_builtins.rs ENFORCE_NEW_FOR_BUILTINS has "Error" only. Repro: throw TypeError('x') -> ESLint only.

reason: In tslib both tools report the same 31 findings, but oxlint's diagnostics carry two label lines (the use and the declaration), so the greedy matcher pairs one with the wrong ESLint report and leaves 3+3 unmatched; the other 3 oxlint-only reports are a secondary false positive on the declaration itself (a parameter or bare var x) of a name re-declared with var in a nested block.
evidence: Re-run on tslib.es6.js: ESLint 31, oxlint 31; the study's matcher leaves ESLint 211 and oxlint 207 unpaired. Repro: function f(b){ var u; for (var i=0;i<b.length;i++){ var u = b[i]; g(u) } } -> oxlint reports the line of 'var u', ESLint nothing. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: The 5 oxlint-only reports are classes that unicorn never visits (var YAMLException = class YAMLException extends Error {...}, _callable(class ArgumentError extends Error {...})): unicorn checks only class declarations and a = class ... assignments, oxlint checks every class; nothing says whether unicorn's narrower scope is intended. The 3 ESLint-only reports are LAG (options-parameter checks, unicorn >=v66).
evidence: unicorn custom-error-definition.js listens only to ClassDeclaration and AssignmentExpression with a ClassExpression on the right (same in v60); its valid tests include const FooError = class extends Error {...}; oxlint custom_error_definition.rs runs on every AstKind::Class. Missing: maintainer intent on class expressions.

reason: oxlint walks only FormalParameter items, so reassigning a rest parameter (...args, ...children, ...plugins) is never reported; all 5 ESLint-only reports are rest parameters.
evidence: Repro: function f(...args) { args = args.reverse(); return args } -> ESLint 'Assignment to function parameter args', oxlint silent (function (x) { x = 1 } is reported by both). no_param_reassign.rs matches AstKind::FormalParameter only. No oxc tracker hit.

reason: unicorn skips any pattern that contains a backslash, while oxlint deliberately unescapes simple escaped characters (/\$$/, /^\[/, /^\\\\\?\\/) and reports them.
evidence: oxlint prefer_string_starts_ends_with.rs has a fixer test turning /^\\\\\?\\/.test(str) into str.startsWith('\\\\?\\') (the exact ignore-package line); escape handling fixed for #10523; unicorn isSimpleString rejects '\\'.

reason: In source-map the same forEach/map(function () {...}, this) finding is reported by oxlint at the start of the call and by ESLint at the this argument 11 lines later; the remaining oxlint-only report is minimatch's non-array orig.filter(pattern, options), already tracked.
evidence: source-map-generator.js pairs 238<->249 and 390<->401; repro: multi-line a.forEach(function(){...}, this) -> ESLint at the this line, oxlint at the call line. Non-array receivers: oxc #18200 (open; unicorn v66 #3219 skips them).

reason: ESLint's member-expression check reads node.property.name without testing computed, so the variable reference _end in source[_end] is reported as if it were a property name (4 reports); oxlint checks only non-computed members, and the var _end declaration is reported by both.
evidence: ESLint 10 no-underscore-dangle.js checkForDanglingUnderscoreInMemberExpression has no node.computed test; repro: var _end = 1; source[_end] -> ESLint reports the declaration and source[_end], oxlint only the declaration.

reason: unicorn v65 allows a bare export {} as a module marker; oxlint still reports it (isexe, uuid, yargs type stubs).
evidence: unicorn v65.0.0 release note 'require-module-specifiers: Allow bare export {} as a module marker (#3001)'. Repro: export {}; -> oxlint 'Empty export specifier is not allowed', ESLint silent.

reason: oxlint treats any if whose parent is an if as an else-if continuation, so if (a) if (b) {} (b is the consequent) adds no depth; ESLint skips only real else-ifs, so js-yaml's if (ch === 33) if (!isNamed) {...} reaches depth 5 only in ESLint.
evidence: Repro: four nested ifs ending in if (d) if (e) {} -> ESLint 'Blocks are nested too deeply (5)', oxlint nothing (with braces both report). max_depth.rs checks only parent_kind == IfStatement; ESLint uses isElseIf (parent.alternate === node). No oxc tracker hit.
